subtitle: The intelligence brief on models, agents, evals & shipping AI products
audience: Product managers building AI/LLM-powered products at startups and tech companies. They ship features on top of foundation models, care about evals, latency, cost, and UX patterns, and need to track model releases and competitor moves. They do NOT need ML research math explained.
in_scope: Foundation-model releases + pricing/capability changes (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral)
Agent frameworks, tool-use, and orchestration patterns
Eval methods, benchmarks, and quality/safety tooling
Notable AI product launches + UX patterns worth copying
AI regulation + policy that changes what PMs can ship
out_scope: Pure ML research papers with no product implication
Hardware/chip deep-dives (unless they change inference cost for app builders)
Enterprise sales-org gossip and funding-round noise without a product angle
Academic theory threads with no shippable takeaway
relevance_gate: Would a PM building an AI product realistically change their roadmap, model choice, evals, or UX after reading this?

tracks.name: Models
tracks.desc: Foundation-model releases, pricing, context-window/capability changes from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral, and challengers.

tracks.name: Agents & Tooling
tracks.desc: Agent frameworks, tool-use, orchestration (LangGraph, MCP, function-calling), and the SDKs PMs build on.

tracks.name: Evals & Quality
tracks.desc: Benchmarks, eval methods, hallucination/safety tooling, and how teams measure LLM output quality.

tracks.name: Products & UX
tracks.desc: Notable AI product launches and interface patterns (chat, inline, agentic) worth studying or copying.

tracks.name: Economics
tracks.desc: Inference cost, latency, pricing moves, and the unit-economics shifts that change what's viable to ship.

tracks.name: Policy
tracks.desc: AI regulation, model-access changes, and platform policy that affects what PMs can legally or practically ship.

tone: Direct, practitioner-to-practitioner, no hype, assumes fluency in shipping software.
